verifications.note: Reuters, via BOE Report (2026-04-29): 'Ares said funds led by its Infrastructure Opportunities strategy would buy 32.4% of Rover...Energy Transfer operates and owns the rest of Rover...Among the assets owned by Traverse is a 35% stake in Rover. Blackstone, which first acquired its stake in Rover in 2017...' -- corroborates Owner1 Energy Transfer (~32.57%, 'the rest') and Owner3 Traverse (35.00%, exact match), but states Blackstone SOLD its 32.4% stake to Ares Management -- contradicts the recorded Owner2 'Blackstone'.

Pipeline & Gas Journal (2026-04-29): 'Ares Management has acquired a 32.4% stake in the Rover natural gas pipeline from Blackstone Energy Transition Partners...The system is operated by an affiliate of Energy Transfer.' Independent second source confirming the same divestiture/acquisition; does not restate Traverse or Energy Transfer's exact percentages.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Cannot confirm the row as currently recorded (Owner1 Energy Transfer 32.57% / Owner2 Blackstone 32.44% / Owner3 Traverse 35.00%) without qualification. Owner1 and Owner3 corroborate: two independent outlets (Reuters via BOE Report, and Pipeline & Gas Journal, both 2026-04-29) state Traverse holds a 35% stake in Rover (exact match to Owner3) and that Energy Transfer 'operates and owns the rest' of the pipeline (consistent with Owner1's 32.57%, not stated as an exact figure). But Owner2 is CONTRADICTED, not confirmed: both sources report Blackstone (via its Energy Transition Partners unit, which first invested in Rover in 2017) SOLD its 32.4% stake to Ares Management (funds led by Ares Infrastructure Opportunities), announced 2026-04-29 -- no source names Blackstone as a current owner as of that date, over four months before this sweep (2026-09-09). The Blackstone press release confirming the same transaction (https://www.blackstone.com/news/press/ares-acquires-stake-in-rover-pipeline-from-blackstone-energy-transition-partners-to-serve-growing-energy-demand-centers-across-north-america/) 403'd on direct fetch with a browser UA; not re-tried via Wayback (archive.org CDX API returned 429 rate-limit) given two other independent, on-topic outlets already corroborate the same divestiture. Also found but not applied: a separate 2026-03-31 transaction (ePointZero agreeing to buy Traverse Midstream itself, the parent company, for $2.25B from The Energy & Minerals Group) -- this changes Traverse's ownership, not Traverse's 35% stake IN Rover, so Owner3='Traverse' stays the correct name of record; flagging only in case the sheet later needs a note. Declining to emit REFS_ADDED because that would falsely re-confirm 'Blackstone' as a current owner; declining to silently substitute 'Ares Management' because changing a recorded value is outside this ref-sourcing unit's scope (Update workflow territory) -- surfacing the contradiction for routing instead. Searched further for an SEC/FERC filing naming the post-transaction ownership split (10-K, EDGAR full-text search 'Rover Pipeline Ares') -- SEC EDGAR returned 403 on the linked ETP 10-K (from 2018, pre-dates the sale in any case) and no newer EDGAR filing was found naming exact post-sale percentages within the time available.
